Belgium joined the Programme in 1963, and over the years has developed it into a Programme, extending its sponsorship to the Multilateral partner organizations with which the Belgian Government stipulated in specific agreements The Junior Professional Officers (JPO) program, also known as the Associate Experts Programme, is a multilateral technical cooperation initiative sponsored by the Directorate General for Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Aid of Belgium. Originating from a United Nations Economic and Social Council resolution adopted in 1961, the JPO program encourages the collaboration of volunteers, financed by their respective countries of origin, to implement development cooperation initiatives and programs. The specific focus of this JPO program is on financing the Junior Professional Officer for the Office of the Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Children and Armed Conflict (OSRSG-CAAC) in New York. The JPO's role involves monitoring and reporting on the situation of children affected by armed conflict in assigned countries, liaising with country task-forces and partners, drafting reports, and following up on situations. The JPO also works towards mainstreaming CAAC at inter-agency meetings at Headquarters and with partners (UNICEF, DPO, and DPPA). They support the Office's work and engagement with the Security Council Working Group on Children and Armed Conflict, its Member States, as well as relevant Permanent Missions in New York and other UN bodies. The JPO also assists in outreach to NGOs, Member States, and other UN partners, liaises with United Nations entities, Member States, and non-United Nations experts on developments relevant to the CAAC agenda, as required. They also participate in thematic research and analysis relevant to the CAAC agenda and support work of teams. The JPO's role requires a strong understanding of key issues related to CAAC, country situations, and the roles of various partners. They must also be knowledgeable about child protection issues in countries affected by conflict, as well as the peace and security nexus of that theme. Additionally, they gain insight into the organization and functions of the peace and security, humanitarian, and development organs of the United Nations and other NGO and civil society organizations concerned with conflict and child protection. The JPO's performance is evaluated based on their duties, responsibilities, and output expectations, which include monitoring and reporting on the situation of children affected by armed conflict, mainstreaming CAAC at inter-agency meetings, supporting the Office's work and engagement with the Security Council Working Group, outreach to NGOs, Member States, and other UN partners, liaising with United Nations entities, participating in thematic research and analysis, and representing the OfficeSpecial Representative of the Secretary-General at conferences, seminars, and academic forums relevant to the work of the Office.
